sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Terraform and Infrastructure-as-Code interview questions cover the tool that provisions most modern cloud infrastructure — providers, resources, state management (and remote state), modules, workspaces, the plan/apply lifecycle, drift detection, secrets handling, and the patterns for multi-environment deployments. Use this page for any DevOps/SRE role where IaC ownership is part of the job spec.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Terraform = **declarative infra**, with state as the source of truth.

- **Providers** — pluggable (AWS, GCP, Azure, K8s, GitHub).
- **State** — `terraform.tfstate`, **remote** in S3+DynamoDB / GCS / Terraform Cloud.
- **Modules** — reusable units; pin versions.
- **Workspaces** — environment isolation (dev / stage / prod).
- **Plan → apply** is the immutable contract.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Terraform core** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **State locking** — non-negotiable for teams; DynamoDB lock for S3 backend.
- **Drift** — out-of-band changes break `plan`; fix with `import` or rebuild.
- **Secrets** — never in `.tf`; pull from a vault data source.
- **Destroy is permanent** — always read the plan before applying.
- **`terraform_remote_state`** — share outputs between root modules.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"State lives remotely with locking, modules are versioned, secrets come from <vault>, environments are split via workspaces, and every change goes plan → review → apply through CI — manual `apply` from a laptop is a smell."*
